Abstract the per-language validity layer over a truth-relation class so a fifth object language inherits it for free. GROUND TRUTH: the tree carries FOUR object languages as separate inductives -- `Formula` (Syntax/Formula.lean:77), `MinusFormula` (MinusLanguage/), `PlusFormula` (PlusLanguage/Formula.lean:90), `StarFormula` (StarLanguage/Formula.lean:104) -- in a strict tower of 6, then 7, then 9 constructors, and the tower is still growing.

THE SEPARATE-INDUCTIVE DECISION IS CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE REVISITED. StarLanguage/README.md records the reason under "Why the operators are not added to PlusFormula": adding the time registers to `PlusFormula` would silently invalidate `stab_state_only` and with it the landed atomization route in Metalogic/Conservativity/Plus/Atomization.lean. Breaking that invariant is the whole point of L-star, and it must break in a separate type. This task does not touch that decision.

But that reason justifies separate TYPES, not separate VALIDITY LAYERS. A survey across Semantics/, PlusLanguage/ and StarLanguage/ finds roughly 658 declarations, with the following appearing once per language at statements identical modulo the formula type and the truth predicate: `TruthAt`, `ValidIn`, `ValidOnFrames`, `TaskFrame.ValidOn`, `.mono`, `.of_forall_total`, `.apply_total`, `Valid.apply`, `swapTemporal`, `timeShift`, and the derived-operator family `neg`/`and`/`or`/`top`/`diamond`/`always`/`allFuture`/`allPast`/`someFuture`/`somePast`/`sometimes`/`dstab`/`interpolates`. Each new language pays for all of them again.

DELIVERABLES, each phase one agent run with lake build green and no new sorry: (1) SCOPE MEASUREMENT FIRST, GATING THE REST: enumerate exactly which declarations are language-agnostic (statement identical modulo the formula type and truth predicate) and which are genuinely language-specific. Report the measured count. The list above is a SURVEY, not a specification -- do not assume it is complete or correct, and correct it where it is wrong. (2) SETTLE THE HARD DESIGN QUESTION BY PROOF, not by assumption: whether one abstraction can cover both point shapes, since L/L-minus/L-plus evaluate at (tau, x) while L-star evaluates at (tau, x, v-vector). If a single abstraction cannot cover both without contortion, say so with the specific obstruction named and abstract only the layers it genuinely does cover -- a partial abstraction with an honest boundary is the successful outcome, an over-general one that fits nothing is not. (3) The class or structure abstracting a truth predicate at a point, with the validity layer written ONCE against it and instantiated per language. (4) EVERY EXISTING PER-LANGUAGE NAME PRESERVED exactly as it stands today. This is a refactor of landed, green, consumed code: no downstream consumer may require editing, and NO theorem may change its statement. If some name cannot be preserved, that is a BLOCKING finding to report, never a rename to perform. (5) Delete the superseded duplicates only after their replacements are green, never before. (6) A stated EXTENSION CONTRACT in the new module's docstring: exactly what a fifth language must supply in order to inherit the validity layer for free. This is the deliverable that pays for the whole refactor, and it must be written from the instantiations actually performed, not aspirationally.

HARD CONSTRAINTS: MUST NOT merge, unify, or weaken the separation between the four formula types -- see StarLanguage/README.md's stated reason above. MUST NOT change any theorem statement. No `sorry`; `lake build` green AND `lake build BimodalTest` green; `scripts/check-module-invariants.sh` exit 0 with axiom baselines unchanged -- a refactor that preserves statements must preserve axiom sets, so any baseline drift is a defect to investigate, not to rebaseline. Never argue by uniform substitution (unsound here). No task numbers under FormalSystem/. If the abstraction cannot be built without violating one of these constraints, report the obstruction and close [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] rather than compromising any of them. TERRITORY: broad by nature -- Semantics/**, PlusLanguage/**, StarLanguage/**, MinusLanguage/**. Sequenced last precisely because it touches everything; it runs only once the content tasks that add to these layers have settled.

Split the ofBase monolith and eliminate the ofPlus-restricted bridge results from TM-star. GROUND TRUTH: `StarAxiom.ofBase (phi : PlusFormula) (ax : PlusAxiom phi) : StarAxiom (ofPlus phi)` (FormalSystem/StarLanguage/Axioms.lean:136) carries ALL 45 TM-plus schemata at `ofPlus` instances only. The research that produced this design established that EXACTLY ONE of those schemata fails schematically over `StarFormula`: `modal_future` (box-phi implies box-G-phi), refuted by `refute_modal_future` (Semantics/StarNonValidities.lean) at phi := recall-1-p implies p. The other 44 are sound at arbitrary phi : StarFormula. One failing schema currently restricts the entire block.

THE VISIBLE COST IS A BRIDGE RESULT, and removing it is the point of this task: `stabNecessitationOfPlus` (StarLanguage/Derivation.lean) is stab-necessitation derivable only at `ofPlus` instances, because MS reaches TM-star only through `ofBase`. The rule is SOUND at every formula -- its restriction is an artifact of axiom packaging, not of mathematics. The originating research report itself gestured at the finer split, recommending that `modal_future` be re-declared under a `RegFree` side condition and noting that `ofBase` already supplies MF at register-free instances.

DELIVERABLES, each phase one agent run with lake build green and no new sorry: (1) VERIFY FIRST, AND THIS GATES EVERYTHING AFTER IT: re-establish BY PROOF that exactly 44 of the 45 TM-plus schemata are sound at arbitrary phi : StarFormula. Do NOT trust the prior count. If more than `modal_future` fails, the split changes shape -- report the true measurement honestly and proceed with whatever it supports; a corrected count is a successful gate, not a failure. (2) Re-declare the schematically-sound schemata directly over `StarFormula`, each with its own constructor mirroring `PlusAxiom`'s corresponding arm, so the two axiom sets stay structurally comparable. (3) Carry `modal_future` ALONE under an explicit register-free side condition. `RegFree` and `IsPureFuture`/`IsPurePast` over `StarFormula` were moved to Non-Goals under the `ofBase` design and must now be defined. (4) RETIRE the monolithic `ofBase`. If a residual embedding arm is still required, it must carry ONLY the schemata that genuinely cannot be stated schematically, and its docstring must name them exhaustively with the reason for each. (5) Re-prove soundness: validity and swap-validity for every newly schematic arm. This is precisely the cost the `ofBase` design avoided; here it is the deliverable, not an obstacle. (6) RETIRE `stabNecessitationOfPlus` in favour of an unrestricted `stabNecessitation`. Delete the restricted name; never keep both. (7) Survey every OTHER `ofPlus`-instance-restricted result reachable from StarLanguage/ and Metalogic/Conservativity/Star/ and widen each one the split covers, rather than widening only the headline. Any that remain restricted must be reported with the specific reason. (8) RE-VERIFY the conservativity results against the new axiom set -- `starDerivable_ofFormula_iff`, `starConservative_of_plusComplete`, `plusIncomplete_of_starNonconservative`. If widening the axiom set breaks a conservativity direction, that is a REAL FINDING about the language and must be reported as a theorem, never silently weakened or worked around.

HARD CONSTRAINTS: no `sorry` -- an unreachable result is recorded as a reasoned exclusion with its obstruction named, never stubbed; never restate a theorem under its own name in weakened form (.claude/rules/plan-compliance.md); never argue by uniform substitution (unsound here); no task numbers under FormalSystem/; `lake build` green, `lake build BimodalTest` green, and `scripts/check-module-invariants.sh` exit 0 with C2/C3/C9/C14/C15/C24/C26 all green -- if a pinned name changes, update the baseline NAME only and never its axiom set. Lift the state-locality fragment to L-plus and retire the atom-restricted stability lemma. GROUND TRUTH: FormalSystem/Semantics/StarStateLocal.lean carries a fully systematic treatment of state-locality for L-star -- the syntactic predicate `StarFormula.StateLocal` by structural recursion over all nine constructors, the semantic property `IsStateLocal`, the soundness induction `isStateLocal_of_stateLocal`, three countermodel exclusions (`not_isStateLocal_someFuture`/`_somePast`/`_timeRecall`), and the headline `stateLocal_starValid_iff_stab`. Notably `isStateLocal_box` is `Iff.rfl` and `stab` is unconditional via `sameStateAt_congr_left`, so the fragment admits box-phi and stab-phi at ARBITRARY phi -- strictly wider than an "every subformula is state-local" reading.

L-plus has no such fragment. It has `stab_state_only` (Semantics/PlusTruth.lean:385) in a different-times shape, plus the ad hoc atom-level consequence `stab_atom_of_atom`. The work that built the L-star fragment identified `stab_atom_of_atom` as the genuine near-miss and excluded it on TERRITORY grounds only, not mathematical ones. The result is that one concept now exists in three incompatible shapes across the tower -- `stab_state_only` (L-plus), `c_stab_state_only` (Metalogic/Independence/CoarsenedModels.lean:325), and the L-star fragment -- and is systematic at exactly one of them.

The L-plus case is STRICTLY EASIER than the case already solved: with no registers, `timeRecall` -- the hardest exclusion -- does not arise, and only `untl`/`snce` should need countermodels.

DELIVERABLES, each phase one agent run with lake build green and no new sorry: (1) `PlusFormula.StateLocal` by structural recursion over all seven constructors, in a new module, named for the property it denotes and not for the theorem that consumes it. Determine BY PROOF which constructors preserve state-locality rather than assuming: `atom`/`bot`/`imp` expected to preserve it, `stab` and `box` expected UNCONDITIONALLY (mirroring `isStateLocal_box`), `untl`/`snce` expected not to. Settle `box` by proof; if it fails here despite holding for L-star, that is a significant finding -- exclude it and record the countermodel. (2) The semantic property and its soundness induction, mirroring StarStateLocal.lean's shape arm for arm so the two modules are structurally comparable rather than merely analogous. (3) Countermodel exclusions for whatever fails. (4) The headline biconditional phi iff stab-phi on the fragment, mirroring `stateLocal_starValid_iff_stab`. (5) RETIRE `stab_atom_of_atom`: generalize it in place, delete the atom-restricted statement, never keep both. Then survey every other atom-restricted statement reachable from PlusTruth.lean and widen each one the new result actually covers -- rather than widening only the headline. (6) RELATE THE THREE NOTIONS EXPLICITLY, which is the deliverable that makes the tower systematic rather than merely parallel: the new module's docstring must state how `PlusFormula.StateLocal` relates to `StarFormula.StateLocal` along `ofPlus` (expected: `ofPlus` preserves it) and how both relate to `c_stab_state_only`. If a transfer lemma along `ofPlus` is provable, prove it; if it is not, record the specific obstruction.

HARD CONSTRAINTS: MUST NOT break the atomization route -- `stab_state_only` is consumed by Metalogic/Conservativity/Plus/Atomization.lean, and generalizing it must not weaken what that consumer needs; verify this explicitly rather than assuming. Never restate a theorem under its old name in weakened form (.claude/rules/plan-compliance.md). Never argue by uniform substitution -- it is unsound in this setting and Metalogic/Independence/DeterminismUndefinable.lean records why. No `sorry`; `lake build` green and `scripts/check-module-invariants.sh` exit 0; no task numbers under FormalSystem/. TERRITORY: Semantics/PlusTruth.lean, a new state-locality module under Semantics/, Semantics/README.md. Does NOT touch StarLanguage/ or StarStateLocal.lean.

active_projects.description:
Build the proof theory for L⋆ and prove conservativity over TM⁺ if it holds. CURRENT STATE: FormalSystem/StarLanguage/ contains only the SEMANTICS of L⋆ = L⁺ + the manuscript's time store/recall operators -- `StarFormula`, `StarTruthAt` over points (τ, x, v⃗), the validity layer, and the determinism results. The names `StarAxiom`, `StarDerivationTree`, `⊢⋆[fc]` and `TM⋆` are RESERVED in StarLanguage/README.md but deliberately unbuilt, because every earlier deliverable was semantic. Consequently neither soundness/completeness for TM⋆ nor any conservativity statement can currently even be STATED. This task closes that gap.

WHY CONSERVATIVITY IS THE POINT: the repository's L⁺ metatheory rests on a conservativity route (Metalogic/Conservativity/ and Conservativity/Plus/). The referee-facing question for L⋆ is whether adding time store and recall proves any NEW L⁺ theorem. The groundwork is already in the tree and must be CONSUMED rather than rebuilt: `ofPlus : PlusFormula → StarFormula` with `ofPlus_injective`, the definitional commutation lemmas (`ofPlus_top`, `ofPlus_neg`, `ofPlus_allFuture`, ...), `ofStarCtx` and `mem_ofStarCtx` (StarLanguage/Formula.lean), and the truth-transfer lemma `starTruthAt_ofPlus` (Semantics/StarTruth.lean). That is precisely the apparatus a conservativity argument consumes.

PHASE 0 IS RESEARCH AND IT GATES EVERYTHING: before a single axiom is written, establish (a) which axiomatization of the store/recall operators the manuscript's def:BLstar-semantics actually licenses, (b) whether TM⋆ is conservative over TM⁺, and (c) whether a completeness proof is reachable at all. Register and hybrid languages frequently resist orthodox completeness arguments and often go undecidable; the literature on hybrid logic with the downarrow binder is the relevant neighbourhood and must be consulted rather than guessed at. Report the finding honestly, a negative one included -- a well-evidenced "not conservative" or "completeness unreachable by this route" is a successful Phase 0, not a failure.

DELIVERABLES, each phase one agent run with lake build green and no new sorry: (1) `StarAxiom` and `StarDerivationTree` with notation `⊢⋆[fc]`, mirroring the shape of the L⁺ proof system (`PlusAxiom`, `PlusDerivationTree`, `⊢⁺[fc]`) so that the two systems are structurally comparable; the embedding of the S/U schemata needs a name that does not read as "of L⁺" (`ofBase` or `ofTM`). (2) SOUNDNESS of TM⋆ over the task-frame semantics. (3) The embedding theorem `⊢⁺[fc] φ → ⊢⋆[fc] (ofPlus φ)`. (4) CONSERVATIVITY, `⊢⋆[fc] (ofPlus φ) → ⊢⁺[fc] φ`, if Phase 0 found it true; if Phase 0 found it FALSE, deliver instead the explicit separating witness formula and state the NON-conservativity theorem, which is an equally publishable result and must not be presented as a shortfall. (5) Completeness ONLY if Phase 0 judged it reachable; otherwise record it as open with the specific obstruction named and the nearest literature results cited, never as a bare "open".

HARD CONSTRAINTS: no `sorry` anywhere -- an unreachable result is recorded as a reasoned exclusion with its obstruction, never stubbed; never argue by uniform substitution (unsound here); never restate a theorem under its own name in weakened form (.claude/rules/plan-compliance.md); do not write to the manuscript or draft manuscript prose; no task numbers under FormalSystem/; keep C2/C3/C14/C15/C24/C26 green. DOCUMENTATION: StarLanguage/README.md's correspondence table gains rows for the proof system and for whatever conservativity verdict lands; the Metalogic README metatheory rows gain TM⋆ with its status (proved, open, or false) stated plainly.
research_questions: AXIOMATIZATION (gates Phase 1 of any plan): which schema set over `StarFormula` does `def:BLstar-semantics` license for the time registers? StarLanguage/README.md states plainly that 'the manuscript supplies no proof system for \BL^\star', so the axioms cannot be transcribed and must be derived from the truth clauses plus the literature. Deliver a schema-by-schema candidate list (K and self-duality for `timeStore`/`timeRecall`; the store/recall cancellations `↑ⁱ↓ⁱφ ↔ φ` and `↓ⁱ↑ⁱφ ↔ ↓ⁱφ`; register/atom commutation `↑ⁱp ↔ p`; the interaction of each register with `□`, `U`, `S` and `⊡`; register-index freshness/renaming side conditions), each with a validity justification checked against the `StarTruthAt` clauses and `StarTruth.timeStore_iff`/`StarTruth.timeRecall_iff` in `FormalSystem/Semantics/StarTruth.lean`, and each rejected candidate with an explicit refutation sketch over a task frame. Ground this in Goranko's temporal logic with reference pointers (the `↑`/`↓` notation the manuscript uses) and the Blackburn-Seligman / Areces-Blackburn-Marx hybrid `↓`-binder axiomatizations; do not guess a set.

PROOF-SYSTEM SHAPE (gates Phases 1-2): does the `PlusAxiom`/`PlusDerivationTree` mirror transfer verbatim to `StarAxiom`/`StarDerivationTree`? Two specific hazards to settle, not assume. (i) `PlusDerivationTree.temporal_duality` requires `swapTemporal`, which is defined on `Syntax/Formula.lean` and `PlusLanguage/Formula.lean` but does NOT exist on `StarFormula` (verified by grep); determine whether `swapTemporal` extends to the registers soundly, and if it does, what the `timeStore`/`timeRecall` arms must be. (ii) In hybrid logic the `↓` binder is a known soundness hazard for necessitation and for uniform substitution (the task description forbids substitution arguments outright); determine whether the 7-rule mirror -- in particular `necessitation`, `temporal_necessitation`, and the empty-context side conditions -- remains sound over register-containing formulas, or whether the rule set must diverge from TM⁺'s. Also settle the naming of the S/U-schemata embedding constructor (`ofBase` vs `ofTM`), given that `PlusAxiom.ofTM` already occupies the latter spelling one level down.

CONSERVATIVITY (decides whether the plan's Phase 4 states conservativity or non-conservativity): is `⊢⋆[fc] (ofPlus φ) → ⊢⁺[fc] φ` true? The route the tree uses for the analogous TM⁺-over-TM row (`Metalogic/Conservativity/Plus/Forward.lean`: star soundness + base completeness + truth transfer) is UNAVAILABLE here, because general nondeterministic TM⁺ completeness is open at every frame class (`Metalogic/Conservativity/Plus/README.md` metatheory table; `docs/theorem-index.md:104`). Determine (a) whether a syntactic route exists -- a register-eliminating translation `StarFormula → PlusFormula` sending each TM⋆ axiom to a TM⁺ theorem (note that naive erasure appears to fail: `↑ⁱ G ↓ⁱ φ → φ` looks valid under seriality but erases to the non-theorem `Gφ → φ`, which needs confirming or refuting), a proof-normalization argument, or a `↓`-free normal-form theorem from the hybrid literature; or (b) whether TM⋆ is NOT conservative, in which case give the explicit separating witness formula with its refutation. Additionally settle the strictly weaker fallback that does appear reachable, and say exactly what it delivers: conservativity of TM⋆ over TM on the `ofPlus ∘ ofFormula` fragment, via TM⋆ soundness + `starValidOn_ofPlus` (`Semantics/StarValidity.lean`) + `plusValidIn_ofFormula_iff` + the TM completeness engines, which needs no TM⁺ completeness.

COMPLETENESS REACHABILITY (decides whether the plan carries a Phase 5 at all): is a completeness proof for TM⋆ reachable with this repository's machinery, or must it be recorded as open with a named obstruction? Note the durable blocker already recorded for the layer below: the countermodels of all four TM completeness engines are deterministic, so `⊡` collapses to the identity on them and no engine transfers to L⁺ as it stands. Determine whether registers make this better or worse, name the specific obstruction, and cite the nearest literature results with their verdicts -- Blackburn-ten Cate on pure-axiom plus non-orthodox-rule completeness for hybrid systems, Areces-Blackburn-Marx on the undecidability and non-compactness of H(↓), Reynolds (2003) and Zanardo (1991) as already cited by the TM⁺ row. A well-evidenced 'not reachable by this route' is a successful answer; a bare 'open' is not.

Prove the strong tense-free stability result and, IF AND ONLY IF it holds, use it to remove the atom restriction from the forward-determinism separation. MOTIVATION: `fn_sentDet_atom (p : Atom)` in FormalSystem/Metalogic/Independence/ForwardDeterministicFrame.lean is restricted to sentence letters, and that restriction is an artifact. Its own docstring gives the real reason -- "an atom's truth depends on nothing but the state at the time of evaluation". The principled closure of that reason is the TENSE-FREE fragment.

EXPLICITLY NOT WANTED: a past-free (or recall-free, or any other ad hoc) fragment. Do not define one, do not prove results about one, and do not fall back to one. An arbitrary restriction is worse than the honest atom-level statement already in the tree. The ONLY acceptable generalization is one carried by a genuinely strong structural result.

THE STRONG RESULT, to be established FIRST and to gate everything after it: for tense-free φ, `φ → ⊡φ` is valid; prove the biconditional `φ ↔ ⊡φ` if it holds, which is the expected outcome since state-locality is a symmetric condition. GROUNDING ALREADY IN THE TREE: L⁺ has `stab_state_only` (Semantics/PlusTruth.lean, indexed from Semantics.lean) -- "⊡φ depends on the world state alone" -- and Metalogic/Independence/CoarsenedModels.lean has the coarsened analogue `c_stab_state_only`. The tense-free result is the companion facing the other way: a tense-free φ is ITSELF state-local, so it cannot distinguish two histories that agree on the state at the evaluation time, which is exactly the class ⊡ quantifies over. Note that 561 recorded `stab_state_only` as FAILING inside a recall scope by design; that is a constraint on the fragment, not an obstacle to the theorem.

DEFINING THE FRAGMENT IS PART OF THE WORK, NOT AN INPUT. Determine BY PROOF which StarFormula constructors preserve state-locality, and define the predicate by structural recursion on StarFormula. Expected: `atom`, `bot`, `imp` preserve it; `stab` preserves it by `stab_state_only`; `timeStore i` preserves it, since storing the current time does not move the evaluation point; `untl` and `snce` do NOT; `timeRecall i` does NOT in general, since it moves evaluation to the stored time vᵢ, which need not be the current time. Whether `box` belongs is an OPEN QUESTION this task must SETTLE rather than assume -- □ quantifies over histories, and if it turns out not to be state-local, exclude it and record a countermodel. Name the predicate for the property it denotes (state-locality / tense-freedom), not for the theorem that consumes it.

THEN, and only if the strong result holds: (a) generalize `fn_sentDet_atom` to every tense-free φ, RETIRING the atom-restricted statement rather than keeping both; (b) survey every other atom-restricted statement reachable from this fragment and widen each one the result actually covers, rather than widening only the headline; (c) KEEP the existing refutations `fn_refutes_sentDet_somePast` and `not_forall_fn_sentDet` untouched -- they are what establish that the fully schematic statement is FALSE, and the new theorem together with those refutations bounds the truth from both sides, which is the publishable shape.

IF THE STRONG RESULT FAILS: record the failure with an explicit countermodel, leave `fn_sentDet_atom` exactly as it stands, and close the task [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS]. Do not substitute a weaker fragment to manufacture a deliverable.

Candidates: (DD); Z1-type backward-induction schemas; the classical H/G axiomatizations of linear discrete/dense/complete flows of time (Burgess 1982 Axioms for tense logic I and II; Burgess 1984 handbook chapter; Kamp 1968; Gabbay-Hodkinson-Reynolds 1994; Prior), adapted to the bimodal setting where □ ranges over all world histories of a single task frame with the MF interaction axiom and every history shares one temporal order (so Log(all task frames) = Log(Discrete) ∩ Log(Dense) and (DD) is a split validity -- see the Halldén analysis in PossibleWorlds tasks 72 and 82, which record that completeness of TM⁻ + (DD) turns on whether TM⁻_f and TM⁻_d axiomatize their classes, both open). Add time addition operator (+) to the bimodal logic TM. φ + ψ is true at (τ, x) iff ∃ y,z with x = y+z, φ true at (τ,y), ψ true at (τ,z). This internalizes the AddCommGroup structure of D into the object language, extending expressive power from FO[<] to FO[<,+] (Presburger arithmetic). Related to arrow logic (Venema), relevant logic (Routley-Meyer ternary frames), and separation logic (BI). Phase 1: add tadd/tsub constructors to Formula, truth clause in semantics. Phase 2: basic axioms (associativity, commutativity, identity, inverse). Phase 3: soundness proofs. Phase 4: interaction with G/H/U/S/□. Completeness (ternary canonical model) and decidability are open research problems — defer to later phases.

Add topological open set (interior) operator for dense and continuous temporal frames. On discrete ℤ the interior is trivial (discrete topology), but on dense ℚ and continuous ℝ it captures neighborhood-stable truth: Int(φ) true at t iff φ holds in an open neighborhood of t. Related to Dynamic Topological Logic (Kremer-Mints 2005), McKinsey-Tarski topological semantics for S4, and Fernandez-Duque intuitionistic temporal logic. Phase 1: add TopologicalSpace instance to TaskFrame for dense/continuous cases. Phase 2: add interior constructor to Formula with truth clause. Phase 3: axioms (S4-like: Int(φ)→φ, Int(φ)→Int(Int(φ))). Phase 4: interaction with temporal operators and S5 □. Note: DTL is not finitely axiomatizable (Fernandez-Duque 2014) — completeness may require non-standard techniques.

THE BOX-FAITHFUL SMALL-MODEL THEOREM.

CLASSIFICATION: OPEN MATHEMATICS. MULTI-MONTH. This is a genuine research problem in the same
category as the audit's R4 "semantic FMP" entry. IT MAY NOT BE RE-DESCRIBED AS ENGINEERING, AND IT
MAY NOT BE MERGED INTO THE BILASSO WIRING TASK OR THE CARRIER-NORMALIZATION TASK. Merging is
precisely how a research problem gets hidden behind an engineering description, and this task
exists partly to prevent that.

DO NOT BEGIN before the BiLasso wiring task and the carrier-normalization task (task 475) are
landed. Those two have standalone value; this one does not, and its cost is dominated by a problem
a two-day literature check might refute outright.

=== LITERATURE GATE -- RUN FIRST, AND IT IS EMPOWERED TO STOP THE TASK ===

Acquire Gabbay, Kurucz, Wolter, Zakharyaschev, *Many-Dimensional Modal Logics* (2003) and read its
temporal-products chapter. IF the two-dimensional `Until`/`Since` case is recorded there as
undecidable or as lacking the finite model property, THIS TASK IS REFUTED and must be REPORTED AS
SUCH rather than attempted. A negative result here is as valuable as a positive one and would
redirect the whole decidability front.

What is already firm from a prior search: products of THREE OR MORE modal logics are undecidable,
with no logic between K x K x K and S5 x S5 x S5 decidable, and S5 x S5 x S5 lacks the finite model
property. What is NOT settled: the two-dimensional case with `Until`/`Since`, which is what this
logic is closest to. Note that TM is in any case NOT a full product -- its second dimension is the
path space of a graph, not an arbitrary set of runs -- so a product-logic result would be evidence,
not a decision.

=== THE TARGET ===

Build `cands : Formula -> List IntPresentation` and prove

    not (ValidDiscrete phi) -> exists P in cands phi, exists w, SatAtState P w phi.neg

This is the SINGLE remaining obligation for decidability of `ValidDiscrete`. Everything else is
already compiled: given this hypothesis, `check`-over-`cands` is equivalent to `ValidDiscrete phi`
and `decidable_of_iff` reads the `Decidable` instance off it. There is no bridge theorem, no
transfer lemma, no enumeration over `Atom`, and no `Fin n`-from-`Finite` extraction anywhere in the
assembly; `check_correct` is the FINAL step.

=== THE CONSTRUCTION (the tractable part) ===

Build `cands phi` from the CLOSURE-TYPE SPACE: subsets of `subformulaClosure phi` satisfying the
local Hintikka conditions, with `step` given by `LocalCoherent`'s `untl`/`snce` unfolding clauses
(`BiLasso/Annotation.lean` already states them, and they relate the label at `t` to the label at
`t` plus-or-minus one only -- i.e. they ARE an adjacency relation), and the valuation read off the
state by deciding atom membership. Every ingredient is `Finset`/`Bool` data with `DecidableEq`.
Two real obligations, neither research-grade:

  1. `fwd`/`bwd` SERIALITY OF THE TYPE GRAPH. Not free: a Hintikka type may have no locally
     coherent successor, forcing an ITERATED PRUNING to a maximal serial subgraph. Standard,
     bounded, fiddly.
  2. INDEXING. `IntPresentation` demands `Fin card` specifically, so the type `Finset` must be
     listed and indexed. Mechanical.

Estimate for this part alone: two to four weeks.

DO NOT instead try "bound `card` by some `presentationBound phi`, then enumerate the presentations
up to that bound". That does not typecheck as stated: `IntPresentation.val : Atom -> Fin card ->
Bool` is a function on the `Infinite` type `Atom`, so presentations of a given `card` are not a
finite collection. Closing that would need a valuation-restriction lemma that is not in the tree.
The formula-indexed candidate list sidesteps the problem rather than solving it.

=== THE CRUX: BOX-FAITHFULNESS (the research part) ===

The `box` clause of `TruthAt` quantifies universally over ALL total histories. Two landed facts
make this a GLOBAL modality rather than a local one:

  - `Truth.box_const` (`Semantics/Truth.lean`): box truth is independent of both the history and
    the time. Its own docstring: "a model has one finite set of box facts, computed once."
  - `Extension.occurrence` (`cor:occurrence`): every state occurs at every time in some total
    history.

That collapse is why `BoxOracleSound P bx` types `bx` as `Formula -> Bool` -- one `Bool` per
formula, per model. It is also the obstruction:

  The box facts of the SOURCE model M and of the TARGET presentation P are each global constants
  of their own model, and they need not agree. P admits every path of its graph. The subgraph of
  types realized in M still generates paths that M does not realize, and along such a path a
  `box chi` true in M can fail. When it fails, the type-map image is no longer a `LocalCoherent`
  annotation, and the transfer breaks.

Restricting `cands phi` to realized-type subgraphs does NOT by itself close this: the subshift
generated by the realized edges properly contains the realized paths. So the residue is a genuine
BOX-FAITHFUL small-model theorem -- in effect a bounded-model property for LTL(Until, Since) over
bi-infinite paths of a graph, PLUS a universal path quantifier over the whole structure.

Is it true? Almost certainly -- the shape is the classical automata-theoretic bounded-model
setting, and the analogous results (CTL*-style satisfiability, LTL with a universal modality) are
decidable with finite/bounded model properties. Is it in reach? Not routinely. Neither Mathlib nor
this tree carries omega-automata, Buchi complementation, or any language-inclusion machinery, so a
Lean proof must be hand-rolled.

=== WHAT TO REUSE ===

`BiLasso/GoodCycle.lean`'s good-cycle argument, `cycleBound`, and `exists_annot_of_truth` are
exactly the fulfilment machinery a hand-rolled proof would reuse. Be clear-eyed that they operate
INSIDE a presentation, not across the model boundary, which is the whole difficulty.

=== DO NOT PROMISE A CHOICE-FREE RESULT ===

`wlem_of_spherical` (`Tests/BimodalTest/Semantics/SphericalFiniteAxiomTest.lean`) derives weak
excluded middle from `Spherical R` at the finite carrier `Bool` over `D = ZZ`, from
`[propext, Quot.sound]` alone. So NO finite-carrier frame with an arbitrarily shaped relation can
be choice-free, on any route. The cost is already paid by `IntPresentation.toTaskFrame`. Any spec
promising choice-freedom here is promising something proved impossible. Note the separate
distinction: `instDecidableSatAtState` COMPUTES (kernel-evaluated `#guard`s prove it) while
measuring `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. Computability and choice-freedom are different
properties.
